posts.body_html: Mike that plant is extremely pretty. I love the way the throat bleeds as someone else mentioned. The shape is also very dynamic and gives the eye a lot to look at. That said, the plant exhibits a very common set of traits - veinless with a blotch from rugelii + white + heavy flava shape influence. If you cruise around FB you will see many, many seedlings along these lines being shown off. They often have AS and / or LW as a parent. It’s a very crowded field of similar iterations and I while I believe this clone is worthy of a designation and being propagated, it isn’t unique enough to register from what I can see in this post.

posts.body_html:
As gotsarrs mentioned, there are some dogs in the registered list, things we would throw out or test new chemicals on! Since this cross looks like many other, similar crosses, you could name it with the proviso that it CAN be seed-raised as long as offspring retain certain traits. I'm thinking of doing that with flava Cinnamon Sticks (cuprea x rubricorpora), but adding only plants with dark red-brown lids and tubes qualify. We raised a ton of seedlings, but only some gave us the color combination we were looking for.

Now, those black plants you gots: after you sell one to me, so I can verify it's not strictly environmental (LOL), that'd be a no-brainer to register.

It's good-looking enough, and as comments indicate, tastes are individual. Maybe the ones worth the hassle of registering are the ones you don't need to ask about.

posts.body_html:
I don't necessarily like my options to the question. It's either amazing or it's compost??!? I don't know the answer.
Question is ... why is this more or less worthy than Legacy? Because Legacy was the first white top/red throat clone??
Everyone says they have a 'version'. I would bet money that someone has a better clone than Legacy. But, is it the first to the finish line or is it the best clone with these traits? This whole thing is bullshit. It's getting as bad as orchids did 15 years ago. Who knows if this one should be registered ... YET. It's not mature . It's definitely NOT compost. Well done Mike. Screw the other opinions. No one asked whether Chas Brew should be registered. If someone comes up with a better clone than Legacy can we strip the cultivar status of Legacy? NO. So ... here we are.

posts.body_html:
Wow, very intriguing feedback, I truly appreciate the honesty, that's what counts here. I'm actually very surprised at how varied these responses are (so far) with this clone, from yes it's a winner, to no there's many look alikes to who knows, we need more time to tell! Personally, I still look at S. leah wilkerson and wonder why everyone in the world wants it, so this is why such threads exist.

To address bogman's comment about questioning a cultivar, I think that's a completely valid point, but it's more of a case by case situation. for example, S. Ellie Wang is unquestionable, nothing out there like it, and the colors are ridiculous, it's easy to grow, easy to color up, pretty much bling-bling by all means. But I've bred plants in the past that I didn't personally deem worthy and they were almost trashed, yet it turns out growers find it very popular! Case and point, S. Leuco burgundy x minor giant 'pink clone' is : sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/438/leuco-burgundy-minor-giant-clone

Bogman: do you think that black Sarracenia I bred (the one that colors up relatively easily) has crappy shape? I heard such feedback and come to think of it, I agree, seems like the shape can be improved. What do you think? If another black plant with better shape is bred, maybe that black one isn't all that and won't stand the test of time.


Anyways, the clone pictured in this thread is a shorter, more compact plant than your every day leah wilkerson x adrian slack, and the lid is slightly disproportionate to the body, meaning it has a pretty big lid! Can it get whiter? Probably, but i don't know. This is the first time I've seen it look worthy of a conversation!

xanthoparmelia-good question, see above for answers that I have today. More to come as the plant is observed. It certainly sticks out amongst the rest of the plants, with that fattie white lid. If I were to deem this cultivar worthy, that would probably be the cultivar name...S. 'fattie white lid' LOL horrible, horrible...i know....

Calen-great feedback, thanks for the insight brah!

Guillaume: Thanks for sharing those pictures! those seedlings look like leah wilkerson x adrian slack, or very similar siblings of Legacy. They're tall and have pretty much very similar shapes to Legacy, but I do see where you're getting at, the plant above may just be another white topped hybrid. The level and extremity of mixed repsonses in this thread have made me even more confused LOL

Rick-awesome response, thanks for sharing!

Keep the comments coming guys, and again, thank you to everyone who has participated in this thread. In fact, I'm so entertained by this forum these days, I have officially stopped watching highly anticipated re-runs of Jerry Springer...buda-boom-CH!!! (crickets chirp after the punchline)
